findings.description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in wheel metadata fetching. User-controlled wheel filename distribution name is directly interpolated into a URL without validation and passed to urlopen(), allowing attackers to redirect requests to arbitrary URLs.
findings.reasoning: The function accepts a `distribution` parameter that originates from parsing wheel filenames (extracted from the first segment of the filename by splitting on '-'). This parameter is directly embedded into an f-string to construct a URL at line 349: `f"https://pypi.org/pypi/{distribution}/json"`. The constructed URL is then passed to `urlopen()` at line 353 without any validation or sanitization. An attacker can craft a malicious wheel filename with a distribution name containing URL scheme prefixes (e.g., "http://attacker.com/endpoint?foo=") or other URL manipulation techniques to redirect the HTTP request to arbitrary URLs, constituting a classic SSRF attack. The noqa comment at line 353 (S310) indicates the code maintainers are aware of the security concern but suppressed the warning, which suggests they may have missed the upstream source of the URL parameter.

evidence.code_context: The Wheel class at src/virtualenv/seed/wheels/util.py extracts the distribution name from wheel filenames: self._parts = path.stem.split('-') and then @property returns self._parts[0]. This is called from release_date_for_wheel_path() at line 323 which passes wheel.distribution to _pypi_get_distribution_info_cached(), which calls _pypi_get_distribution_info() at line 348 with the unvalidated distribution name.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: Distribution name flows from: wheel filename → Wheel._parts[0] → wheel.distribution → _pypi_get_distribution_info_cached(distribution) → _pypi_get_distribution_info(distribution) → f-string URL construction at line 349 → urlopen(url) at line 353. No sanitization or validation occurs at any step.
evidence.attack_vector: An attacker can create a malicious wheel file with a crafted filename such as 'http://attacker.com/endpoint?foo-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl' or '@attacker.com#-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl' to manipulate the constructed URL to point to arbitrary locations.
evidence.mitigations_absent: No URL validation, no whitelisting of allowed distribution names, no hostname validation after URL construction.
